back: A shift of the whole supply curve caused by a factor other than the good's own price.

front: What is a **change in quantity supplied**?
back: A movement along the supply curve caused by a change in the good's own price (extension or contraction).

front: Which way does the supply curve shift for a **decrease** in supply?
back: To the left: less is supplied at every price.
Costs of production; technology; weather; number of firms; taxes and subsidies; prices of other goods; expectations.

front: What is the effect of an indirect tax on supply?
back: It raises costs, so supply decreases (the curve shifts left).

front: What is the effect of a subsidy on supply?
back: It lowers costs, so supply increases (the curve shifts right).
When producing one good also produces another, e.g. beef and hides; more of one means more of the other.

front: How does a drought affect the supply of maize?
back: It decreases supply: less is harvested at every price (shift left).

front: Why does better technology increase supply?
back: It lowers the cost of producing each unit, so firms can profitably supply more at every price.
